title: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
summary: Ketkä asks which people or who several people are. Ketkä te olette? — Me olemme opettajia.
targetSkills: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
prerequisiteSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
objectives: Ask who several people are with ketkä.
Change the group perspective correctly when giving an identity reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
Ketkä asks which people or who several people are. Use plural olla forms: Ketkä te olette? (“Who are you?” addressed to a group).
keyPoints: Do not use singular kuka when asking for the identities of several people.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: When a group is addressed as te, its reply uses me olemme (“we are”). When both speakers mean another group, keep he ovat (“they are”). Profession words describing the members normally take the plural partitive: opettajia (“teachers”). The complete profession forms are provided here. In a role game, Ketkä me olemme? (“Who are we?”) receives Te olette… (“You are…” addressed to the group).
A natural short reply to “Ketkä te olette?” is “Opettajia.” (“Teachers.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
When a group's identity has been guessed incorrectly, emme ole rejects that description. The second sentence supplies who the group actually are.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: A group's reply about itself uses me olemme, not te olette.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: olemme means we are here. Olla has the we-form olemme: ole- + -mme.
ovat means are here. Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.
olette means you are here. Olla has the plural you-form olette: ole- + -tte.
keyPoints: A group's reply about itself uses me olemme, not te olette.

examples.finnish: Me emme ole opettajia. Me olemme opiskelijoita.
examples.english: We are not teachers. We are students.
steps: Me: we; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Me includes the speaker and at least one other person.
emme: we do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Emme is the plural first-person negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
opettajia: teachers; identity or category given after olla. Opettaja takes the plural partitive form opettajia: replace the final a with i and add a.
olemme: we are; verb (the action or state). Olla has the we-form olemme: ole- + -mme.
opiskelijoita: students; identity or category given after olla. Opiskelija has the taught plural partitive opiskelijoita: opiskelij- + -oita.
